verdict: Changes needed. The lifecycle and ownership inside RecordsApplication hold up: onBeforeStart runs while the running gate is off, onStart shows the layout only after both children are ready, the list's owner listeners are removed when it is destroyed, and the collection is disposed on stop. The one real defect is in main.js: showStartError treats every rejected start as a failure the user should see. That includes starts that were cancelled or replaced by a newer one. The last cross-browser rerun is also still pending.
blockingIssues: main.js showStartError runs even for starts that are no longer current. If Retry is clicked while a start or restart is still loading, the older promise may reject with an AbortError or a late network error. Its handler then runs `await application.stop()`, which cancels the new, correct start, and shows ErrorView. Close during loading has the same problem: stop() aborts the fetch, the rejection reaches showStartError, and ErrorView appears after the user closed the feature. Fix: ignore AbortError, and ignore errors from any start that is no longer the latest (a request token or a check against the app's current start). Only stop and show the error for the current, non-aborted attempt. This is not a blocker only if Application.start/restart already resolve or stay pending when a start is replaced or stopped. The notes don't say which, so confirm it in the source.
The final cross-browser rerun after the EmptyDetailView/DetailView split, and the mutation reruns, are still queued. Don't treat this as mergeable until they pass.
risks: If Application.stop() does not empty its region, Close leaves the RecordsLayout and its list on screen, bound to a destroyed collection. Clicking a row would then call state.set while the app is stopped. The running gate blocks showDetail, but the stale UI stays. Check stop's region behaviour.

If prepareStart resolves just before an abort lands, onStart never runs and the returned Collection is never assigned to this.records, so it is never destroyed. That's harmless here (plain DTO models), but the pattern breaks if an adapter later returns a Collection that owns resources.

showDetail assumes this.records and getView() exist whenever the state handler fires. That relies entirely on the running flag turning on at or after onStart. If the framework ever turns it on before onStart, a selection change during start would throw.
Application.showView(new ErrorView()) is called on a stopped app. Make sure the stopped app doesn't take ownership of the view in a way the next start's onBeforeStart showView won't clean up.
incorrectAssumptions: The review assumes a rejected start()/restart() always means 'show the error'. Cancelled and superseded starts break that assumption unless the framework swallows them.
'actual fetch abort' is tested, but the notes don't say the UI reaction to the abort is checked. A test that the abort happened doesn't show the user avoids seeing ErrorView.
missingTests: Click Retry twice quickly, or restart while the first start is still loading: the final UI shows the successful layout, not ErrorView, and the second start isn't stopped.
Close while loading: no ErrorView, the region ends empty or in its defined closed state, and no console.error.
An older start fails after a newer restart has already begun: the failure is ignored.
After Close, the region content matches the defined closed state, and clicking a leftover row (if any remain) does nothing and doesn't throw.
Open while already running or starting does nothing: no second fetch, and the layout isn't replaced.
simplifications: Guard in one place: `const run = fn => { const p = fn(); latest = p; p.catch(e => { if (p !== latest || e?.name === 'AbortError') return; showStartError(e); }); }`. Use it for the initial start, Open and Retry. This avoids spreading abort checks across the handlers.
The `this.listenTo(list, 'destroy', ...)` cleanup is fine as it is. Don't generalise it into a helper for this example.
nextSteps: Check in the Application source what start() and restart() promises do when a start is replaced or stopped. If they reject, add the stale/abort guard in main.js.
Add the three race tests: double Retry, Close while loading, and a late failure from an old start.
Check whether stop() empties the region and assert the closed state in a test.
Finish the pending cross-browser and mutation reruns on the final code before merging.
Out of scope (optional later work): in-place refresh, and making DetailView and the count re-render on changes.
